goal.text: Asher's stated goal is for the company to run 90-95% autonomously.

figure.intro: These measures follow approved work through acceptance and release, and show where agent time goes. They are not a company autonomy rate: the founder's time is not yet measured.

metrics.label: Outcomes accepted October 13–16 that were released to their destination within 72 hours
metrics.blurb: Since October 13, the founder's accept releases the work: merged, deployed or sent. This counts accepted work with a recorded release within 72 hours. One release waited on a system update; one was never scheduled.
metrics.method: review accept events 2026-10-13T21:00Z – 2026-10-16T22:00Z paired with owner_release_done within 72 h. Release is the agent's recorded release, not an independent check that a user received it.

metrics.label: Agent working minutes on client and product projects, October 13–16
metrics.shortLabel: Agent time on clients and products
metrics.blurb: Since October 13, the share of agents' working minutes spent on client projects and our own products rather than on the system that runs the company.
metrics.method: Owner-session minutes clipped to 2026-10-13T21:00Z – 2026-10-16T22:00Z, by project category (client and product vs internal).

metrics.label: Outcomes approved October 1–13 that the founder accepted by the end of that window
metrics.blurb: Every piece of work approved in our first two-week trial (October 1–13), followed to the trial's end: how much the founder accepted. Accepted means he took a demo-ready result, not that it reached anyone.
metrics.method: Cohort of outcome_approved events 2026-10-01T04:00Z to 2026-10-13T21:00Z; accepted = status accepted (version-control history) or a review accept action before the cutoff.
